After a upgrade from L10 to L11 (followed by L12) we're running into issues highlighted here: <https://laravel.com/docs/11.x/upgrade#modifying-columns>

I'm OK with fixing this but I wondered why this change was made.

What could be the reason?
To be more explicit

Think of it this way.

Next time you want to know the db state, you can look at the last migration and it will TELL you the actual state of that column. As opposed to only being the delta/change.

Cause if it's just the change, you have to start hunting through migrations to add it all up.
On the flip side, I have to get the last migration to define or alter the column and copy it forward.
True, but you probably would have been looking at the column definition anyways to make sure you know where you're starting from

Right, the framework used to use a package that looked at the column first to determine what needed to change. That package is no longer needed and it’s up to you to know about your database instead of it being inferred.

It's also helpful in a specific situation like when I'm reviewing code for another project that I'm not as familiar with. The PR has the change and I know, now, what the full column definition will be after this migration is run. Super helpful when I'm not on that project daily to be familiar with it
If you subscribe to down migrations to, it's super clear as to what it was and what you're changing

Maybe our codebase is old enough to make it seem painful.

I tend to look at the column in the DB to work out what's going on.

I'm sticking with the opinion that I prefer the old way.
